claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 7 years old and does not live with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 7 (under 16)
  - Claimant contributes £50.00/week towards child's upkeep (>= £26.05) and no other claimaint has priority
  - Child in local authority care for 12 weeks (>8) and does not spend 24+ hours/week at home
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a child, Alex, who is 7 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask you the next question to assess your eligibility.

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after them - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards their upkeep - things like clothes, pocket money, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To clarify further:

How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or in lump sums)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to ensure I have a complete picture.

Who does Alex currently live with?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in local authority care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask a couple more questions about Alex's situation.

How long has Alex been in local authority care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

Does Alex spend any regular time at home with you each week? For example, do they spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you, or at least 2 nights in a row each week, or 7 days or more in a row at home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't come home to stay with me. They're at the care home full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I need to ask one final question:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While Alex is 7 years old (under 16) and you live in the UK, Alex has been in local authority care for several months, which is more than the 8-week time limit. According to the Child Benefit rules, payments are usually affected after a child has been in care for more than 8 weeks.

There is an exception that allows you to continue receiving Child Benefit for a child in care if they spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you. However, since Alex is at the care home full-time and doesn't come home to stay with you, this exception doesn't apply to your situation.

Although you do contribute £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep, the financial contribution exception specifically applies to children in hospital or residential accommodation, not to children in local authority care.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If Alex's circumstances change in the future - for example, if they start spending regular time at home with you - you may want to contact HMRC to reassess your eligibility.
